newsitem.title: PERU: SOCCER-NEWCOMERS SPORTING CRISTAL AIM TO CRUSH CRUZEIRO.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-NEWCOMERS SPORTING CRISTAL AIM TO CRUSH CRUZEIRO.

text.p: Newcomers to the final of the Libertadores Cup, Peru's Sporting Cristal will host Brazil's Cruzeiro in the first leg of South America's premier club competition on Wednesday, hoping to extend their giant-killing streak.

Cristal, who have recorded shock wins over Argentina's powerhouses Velez Sarsfield and Racing Club this year, are the first Peruvian team to reach the finals in 25 years and are bidding to become their country's first winner of the 38-year-old cup.

Cruzeiro, playing in the final for the third time, are former holders. But their last appearance at this stage was two decades ago and they are dogged by a more recent memory -- defeat earlier this season when they first played Cristal in Lima.

The Peruvians are also buoyed by a spectacular semifinal win against Racing when they came from behind to beat the Argentines 6-4 on aggregate. Cruzeiro needed a penalty shootout to squeeze past Chile's Colo Colo.
"Cristal's campaign has been brilliant, eliminating two huge clubs like Velez and Racing. But we are Cruzeiro and we are geared up to win," Brazilian coach Paulo Autori said.
Cristal's exciting run to the final has persuaded coach Sergio Markarian to set aside the familiar, cautious tactics of a first leg. He has promised aggressive play.
"I simply want to win the match and play it as if it were the only match. To my mind there are two games of sudden death," Markarian said.
Despite the suspension of stars, Prince Amoako of Ghana and local goalscoring hero Julio Rivera, the coach said: "We are going to go out respectful but confident because we know we can win."
The match in Lima's humid National Stadium before a 45,000 crowd is due to kick off at 8.00 p.m. local time Wednesday (0100 GMT Thursday).
The winner of the final will represent South America in the Intercontinental Cup against Germany's Borussia Dortmund -- winners of the European Cup.

The Latins are holders of the one-off match between the two continents after River Plate of Argentina beat Italy's Juventus last year in the game that traditionally decides the world's best club side.

Teams (Probable): Sporting Cristal - Julio Cesar Balerio, Marcelo Asteggiano, Manuel Marengo, Miguel Rebosio, Martin Vasquez, Eric Torres, Jorge Soto, Nolberto Solano, Pedro Garay, Julio Andrade Julinho, Alberto Bonnet
Cruzeiro: Dida, Vitor, Gelson, Gottardo, Nonato, Fabinho, Ricardinho, Donizete, Palinha, Cleisson, Marcelo.
